admission.justification: Shared declaration and live-registration tests jointly prevent a later tool owner from silently growing the repeated context or dropping the only route to complete calling instructions.

applicability: Description text and published input-schema descriptions advertised by the product's registered MCP tool surface.
conditions: Ordinary finalized tool descriptions end with the skill or reference that carries their longer explanation.
A still-interim-owned tool keeps its recorded landing length until its answer-table owner makes the row final.
The retained dispatch_agent description keeps its named transition length until its replacement and removal land together.
exclusions: Harness-native tools and user-configured non-product servers.
Tool answer-token ceilings, which the answer guard owns separately.
An assertion that all models in an arbitrary current build already pass the schema-description check.

evidence: MIK-R112@v1 rule 7, current primary SHA c98e45347f34e81db278c0341ecc7626d6638da0a3b51688d2fa861783a1971f; current source read after completed L50 sync at code HEAD 00d6b4d48ad47e076a87c594ff85456ef80978ef. The proof entries name the checks and their facets, not a fresh Curator test run or a claim that foreign overlong models are repaired. The Worker's and Reviewer's exact historical CODE PASS and failed-test evidence remain separate.

statement: A finalized registered-tool description is bounded to 600 characters and ends by naming an openable longer explanation; published input-schema descriptions are bounded to 120 characters, while explicitly interim-owned tools and the retained dispatch_agent description keep their pinned transition lengths until their owning change lands.
